idle-1.note: M1b 0.17 % CPU / 100 MB; P1 0.053 % / 77 MB. Time Profiler over 30 s: 17 ms of CPU (pod metrics decode, sidebar badge refresh); no Moorings work at idle. fds 73 vs 61 in M1b: Moorings (merged after M1b) watches the explicit test kubeconfig with an FSEventStream with kFSEventStreamCreateFlagWatchRoot, which holds one directory fd per path component of .testcluster (7 DIR fds); flat over the run.

hidden.note: M1b 0.013 % / 72 MB; P1 0.0 % / 55 MB, 0.002 wakeups/s. connectedMinutesPct 10: the stores stop once the window closes (expected); the run was connected during the settle period. fds +11 vs M1b: the Moorings watch-root fds (see idle-1).

testLaunch.note: perf-launch.swift, 7 runs, idle-1 without -WHPerfKeepVisible (the regular launch path). coldLaunchP90Sec is now nearest rank: M1b's own runs give 0.303 s by nearest rank (0.278 s was the 6th of 7), so 0.323 s is +7 %. firstContentP90Sec (new): launch to the FirstContent marker (workspace instead of the Starting view); the gap to the window is the explicit test kubeconfig read on a utility queue (main thread idle after 0.3 s in the launch profile). With -WHPerfKeepVisible the window itself appears later (0.66 s p90: it is ordered out and in to join all Spaces), so that run was not recorded.

soak-5.note: 60 minutes with leaks on the final P1 build, window visible in every minute. footprintGrowthMB is the P1 definition (low of the last whole-cycle window minus the low of the window starting at minute 10). The log ring fills at about minute 33 (20,000 lines at 10 lines/s); after that the table keeps up to 2,000 dropped lines as slack rows. CPU per 10-minute segment: 4.33, 4.37, 4.38, 4.42, 4.41, 4.52 %. cpuAvgPct includes the 5-minute navigation cycle (ConfigMaps 2,000 rows) and the log follow; the soak budgets are memory growth, leaks, threads and fds.

firstRun.note: The first 60-minute P1 soak, on the build before the buffer-sharing fix (f8c34c3): the table and the model shared the line array, so each sync copied all lines and CPU grew with the line count. CPU per 10-minute segment: 4.42, 4.64, 5.01, 5.22, 5.24, 5.40 %.

soak-5.buildNote: Recorded on f8c34c3. The later changes (appendOnly prefix check, untracked read of the model lines, reload on a source switch, dead state removed, the jump to the oldest line limited to front trims, constant minimums limited to resource lists and the log screen) do not change what a followed log does per update: the soak follows one pod with follow on, never switches source, toggles matching lines or trims while scrolled away, and its screens (Pods list, log screen) keep the constant minimum.
soak-5.growthNote: footprintGrowthMB re-summarised from the same CSV with the final metric (lows 115 -> 117 MB scaled from the time between the lows to the 50 minutes from minute 10: +2.6 MB; +2.0 unscaled). The first run measures -1.0 MB either way.

environment.display: another app was full screen on the active Space for the whole pass; visible scenarios ran with -WHPerfKeepVisible YES (accessory app, window floating on every Space) and the sampler checked the app's own visibility verdict every minute

logFollowCpu.scenario: soak-5 with the window visible, follow of the chatter pod (10 lines/s), top over 60-90 s after a 60 s settle
logFollowCpu.note: 8.2 %: every flush re-rendered the whole SwiftUI log screen twice and every SwiftUI update re-measured the column's minimum size (NSHostingView.minSize, ~7 ms). After the split (child views, throttled footer, model syncs itself, table follows the model, constant column minimums): 4.5 %; the following table updating twice a second: 3.6 % at the start of a follow. With a full ring the old front-drop path (removeRows + insertRows) cost 8-9 %; with the slack rows it costs the same as a growing ring. What remains is about 8 ms of AppKit per table update (CA commit of the layer tree, tracking areas, window layout); drawing itself is about 1 ms per update. Measurements taken while the window was occluded (the first 'after' runs, before the sampler checked visibility) were discarded.

note: P1: the Instruments pass (Time Profiler on idle-1, hidden, the soak's log follow and a launch; Leaks via leaks at the end of each soak), the fixes listed per scenario, a sampler that fails runs that were not connected or not visible, and soak growth measured over whole cycles. Regressions against M1b, justified: fds (idle-1, hidden, soak-5: the Moorings watch-root directory fds, merged after M1b); testLaunch (nearest-rank p90, M1b's runs give 0.303 s that way); soak-5 samples/minutes (60 instead of 30 minutes); soak-5 idleWakeupsPerSec 2.28 vs 0.28 (the visible log follow now really draws: 4 Hz model sync and 2 Hz table updates; M1b's soak was never checked for visibility); soak-5 footprintLastMB 132 vs 110 and fdsOverBaseline 5 vs 3 (phase of the 5-minute sawtooth at the last sample, and a 60-minute run whose ring fills at minute 33 where M1b's 30-minute run never filled it).
